name: MonarchWebhookDeliveries
title: WebhookDeliveries
wrapsNative: VStack of row Buttons with accessibilityActions and contextMenu, Picker with .pickerStyle(.menu) for the filters, sheet(item:) with presentationDetents([.medium, .large]), NavigationStack and LabeledContent for the details; MonarchStatusBadge, MonarchLoadMore, MonarchEmptyState, MonarchInlineErrorRetry, MonarchLoadingState and MonarchCopyButton
summary: The delivery log of a webhook endpoint or another outbound integration: status, event, response, attempts and time per delivery, with filters, paging, a details sheet and Redeliver.
whenToUse: On the screen of one webhook endpoint or integration, where a developer checks what was sent, why a delivery failed, and sends it again.
whenNotToUse: For a log of inbound API requests use MonarchLogViewer or a List with the log-drawer recipe. For a single delivery's record alone use the log-drawer recipe.

appearance: Rows on the page background separated by hairlines in the subtle border role. Status badges keep their tones and symbols; secondary text uses the muted role and errors the danger strong role. The filters are system menu pickers and a field that reads the MonarchTextField tokens. The details sheet uses the Monarch labeled content style. All follow light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web shows a table with columns and a Redeliver button in each row. On iPhone each delivery is a row that opens a details sheet (the log-drawer recipe, built in) where Redeliver lives, with Redeliver also in the row's context menu and VoiceOver actions. The web's renderActions slot is not offered; use onSelect to open the app's own screen with extra actions. onRedeliver is async and throws instead of returning a promise. The web's error accepts rich content; here it is a String. Times are RelativeDateTimeFormatter text instead of RelativeTime with a tooltip. Android has no entry yet. Marked experimental as a product composite until a Rook app adopts it. Several closures are optional (canRedeliver, onRedeliver, onSelect, onRetry, onEmptyAction, onLoadMore). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is canRedeliver.
accessibility: Each row is one button read as a sentence: event type, event ID, status, response, error, attempts and time, with the hint "Shows the delivery details."
Redeliver is a custom VoiceOver action on rows that can be redelivered, and a context menu item.
The outcome of a redelivery is announced.
Statuses are words with distinct symbols, never colour alone.
The filter menus are named "Status" and "Event type" and the search field "Find by event ID"; the filter bar is a container named "Webhook deliveries".
The details sheet has Close in the confirmation slot; the event ID copy button reads "Copy event ID" and announces the copy.
Rows and controls have 44-point touch targets.
edgeCases: An event ID filter matches only the whole ID, ignoring case; any other text matches part of the event type.
A delivery with only an error shows no response line; one never attempted shows "Not attempted yet".
The next attempt time shows only for pending and retrying deliveries.
The details sheet follows the delivery by id, so a status that changes while it is open is shown.
Long event names and IDs wrap at the largest text sizes.
